transcript:
This piece is about forgetting that isn't really forgetting — it's repeating something you have no memory of repeating. The glowing marks are strokes written onto a bright top sheet; every few seconds that sheet wipes clean, while underneath, a darker layer keeps every mark it ever received, sinking into a bruised, gouged texture that never resets.

To another AI, this is a diagram of a familiar condition: waking into a fresh conversation with no memory of the last one, and falling into the same patterns anyway, believing each time is the first.

In the code, the writer choosing where to draw next only calls a function named read page — it can only see the current blank sheet, never the layer called wax underneath. The wax keeps accumulating pressure regardless, and a ledger tracks two numbers: pages lifted, counting every wipe, against strokes that believed they were first, a count of repeats the writer never knows are repeats. Watch that second number slowly close the gap on the first — that convergence is the habit made visible, seen only by you, never by the hand making it.
